tennis_critical: All four Grand Slams use a 10-POINT tiebreak at 6-6 in the deciding set (since 2022, in force 2026). No Slam final set is open-ended: Bo5 caps at 65 games, Bo3 at 39.
Tiebreak counts as ONE game - per-set max is 13 games, not 12.
Best-of-5 ONLY in men's singles main draw at Slams. Slam QUALIFYING and juniors are Bo3. NO women's event uses Bo5 - a WTA Bo5 market is a corrupt feed, suppress it.
Doubles use a 10-point match tiebreak instead of a 3rd set (counts as 1 game): doubles cap at 27 games. Singles totals models over-bet doubles systematically.

RETIREMENT: three conventions exist (all-void / one-ball-served / first-set-completed) and books differ. Under ALL of them totals/handicaps/correct-score VOID unless determined. Betwinner's own terms MUST be read.
Surface change: some books void ALL bets, others let them stand - opposite outcomes, verify Betwinner's rule.
No-ad scoring (doubles, many Challengers) raises underdog break probability - favourite handicaps worth less than ad-scoring equivalent.
table_tennis_critical: Game to 11 win-by-2: per-game totals are open-ended above 21 (deuce tail).

Fast circuits (Liga Pro, TT Cup, TT Elite, Setka) are Bo5 - but playoffs/finals sometimes Bo7. FORMAT MUST BE READ PER MATCH, never inherited from league name - the highest-frequency TT mispricing trap.
From 10-10 service alternates every point - serve advantage neutralised, deuce games near coin-flip.
Points handicap and games handicap are NOT interchangeable (3-0 yields far fewer points than 3-2).
Self-umpired circuits: manual score feeds, duplicate player names, late substitutions - treat as high-staleness by default.
Retirement rates on amateur circuits EXCEED tour tennis - larger EV drag from voids.
